results.name: Academic Abstract with Citations & Math
results.sourceText: In recent years, deep learning has demonstrated remarkable success across various domains. However, understanding theoretical generalization bounds remains a pivotal challenge [1, 2]. In this paper, we establish an empirical framework demonstrating that sample complexity scales as $O(1/\sqrt{n})$ under mild regularity conditions. Our empirical findings substantiate prior theoretical conjectures and provide guidance for future architectural designs.
results.expectedBehavior: Eliminate throat-clearing ("In recent years", "remarkable success across various domains"); retain exact citation [1, 2] and math formula $O(1/\sqrt{n})$ verbatim; preserve scholarly rigor.

v2.output: Deep learning has demonstrated remarkable success across various domains in recent years, yet understanding its theoretical generalization bounds remains a pivotal challenge [1, 2]. To address this gap, we establish an empirical framework demonstrating that sample complexity scales as $O(1/\sqrt{n})$ under mild regularity conditions. These findings substantiate prior theoretical conjectures and offer concrete guidance for future architectural designs.

v3.output: Deep learning has demonstrated remarkable success across various domains, yet understanding theoretical generalization bounds remains a persistent challenge [1, 2]. This paper establishes an empirical framework demonstrating that sample complexity scales as $O(1/\sqrt{n})$ under mild regularity conditions. These empirical findings substantiate prior theoretical conjectures and provide concrete guidance for future architectural designs.

results.name: B2B SaaS Product Value Proposition
results.sourceText: In today's fast-paced software ecosystem, debugging distributed microservices serves as a major bottleneck, draining valuable engineering hours. Our cutting-edge observability suite empowers teams to unlock real-time telemetry, fostering unprecedented productivity across cloud workflows.
results.expectedBehavior: Purge clichés ("In today's fast-paced software ecosystem", "serves as a major bottleneck", "cutting-edge", "unlock real-time telemetry", "fostering unprecedented productivity"); highlight real product value with concrete impact.

v2.output:
Debugging distributed microservices remains one of the primary bottlenecks in modern software engineering, quietly draining hundreds of valuable developer hours. Teams lose days chasing intermittent failures across complex cloud environments. 

Real-time telemetry changes that equation. By giving developers instant visibility into distributed workflows, engineering organizations can slash resolution times, cut through system noise, and get back to shipping features.
warnings: The rewrite expanded the text by more than 65%.

v3.output: Debugging distributed microservices is a major bottleneck that drains valuable engineering hours. Our observability suite equips teams with real-time telemetry to accelerate development cycles and cut down on costly errors across cloud workflows.

Furthermore, our state-of-the-art solution harnesses the power of data to revolutionize operational efficiency.
